title: Standardize client-server retry choreography with opaque idempotency tokens and hedged-fanout controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a single, backward-compatible retry choreography across server-side services and client SDKs that uses opaque idempotency tokens, hedged request controls, and SLO-aware backoff budgets. This work unifies semantics for retries, hedged fanout, timeouts, and observability so caller libraries and runtime components make compatible decisions during multi-region failover and surge conditions.
background: Multiple services and SDKs currently implement divergent retry semantics: different idempotency header names and token formats, inconsistent hedged-request thresholds, and mismatched timeout windows. This has caused duplicate processing incidents during regional failovers and unclear telemetry when retries mask underlying capacity issues. Previous tickets standardized pieces (retry backoff, idempotency headers) but left gaps in end-to-end choreography and migration paths for existing clients.
goals: Publish a canonical retry choreography contract (headers, token lifecycle, hedged fanout bounds) consumable by the runtime and all official SDKs
Introduce an opaque Idempotency Token (IdTok) format and header name that avoids application-level semantics and can be rotated transparently
Implement SLO-aware admission for hedged requests at the gateway/runtime to limit fanout under load and prefer graceful load shedding
Ship SDK v2.1 compat layer that sets IdTok, honors server hedging hints, and exposes opt-in deterministic retries for idempotent operations
Provide migration guidance, rollout tooling (feature flags, canary gating), and observability to detect duplicate side-effects
non_goals: Changing application-level idempotency semantics (business logic) for existing services
Enforcing idempotency tokens for every legacy endpoint during initial rollout
Extensive changes to third-party client libraries outside official SDKs
design_decisions: IdTok is opaque: a base64 URL-safe string with a short HMAC prefix for early validation; servers MUST treat it as opaque and not parse semantics
Canonical header: X-Redwood-Idtok; SDKs will add X-Redwood-Idtok-Signature for optional client-side signing during enterprise deployment

Hedging policy: runtime exposes a per-route hedging hint header (X-Redwood-Hedge-Hint) with three enumerated values: allow, prefer, disallow. The runtime enforces global hedging budgets tied to SLO tokens.

SLO-aware backoff governor: retries are budgeted against an SLO token bucket per-customer and per-region; when budget low, gateway reduces hedged fanout and signals SDKs to fall back to single-try with exponential backoff
Backward compatibility: if no IdTok present, server treats request as non-idempotent and defaults to non-hedged single-try unless route metadata marks it safe
implementation_tasks: Design and finalize IdTok format and header RFC (doc/confluence) - owner: Liam
Runtime: add hedging governor and per-route hedging hint propagation - owner: Platform Infra
Gateway: implement SLO-token enforcement and hedging budget checks - owner: Edge Team
SDKs (python/node/go): add IdTok generation API, automatic attachment, and hedging hint handling - owner: SDK Team
Telemetry: add deduplicated side-effect counter, retry-attribution traces, and hedged-fanout histogram to the console - owner: Observability
Migration: create canary workflow and feature flag to enable IdTok on a per-service basis - owner: Release Eng
Docs: migration guide, sample code, and runbook for incident responders - owner: DX Team
rollback_plan: Toggle feature flag to disable IdTok insertion at gateway/SDK; runtime hedging governor has an emergency disable switch. If duplicate side-effects increase above safety threshold, immediately disable hedging at gateway and revert SDK rollout to previous minor version.
rollout_plan: Week 0: RFC review and approval; create feature flag and telemetry dashboards
Week 1-2: Implement runtime hedging governor behind feature flag; unit and integration tests
Week 3: SDK beta release to internal teams and opt-in customers; run Chaos scenarios in staging
Week 4: Enable IdTok on low-risk routes with canary percentage 1% -> 10% -> 50% while watching duplicate side-effect and SLO metrics
Week 5-6: Incremental expansion to all routes; deprecate legacy header after 90 days with warning logs
acceptance_criteria: Canonical RFC published and reviewed by security, infra, and SDK leads
Runtime hedging governor enforces per-customer hedging budgets and logs enforced actions
SDKs released with IdTok behavior and hedging hint handling; integration tests pass against runtime staging
Console dashboards show hedged-fanout histograms and deduplicated side-effect metric; alert to P1 when duplication rate > 0.1% for high-throughput routes
Migration runbook validated with one internal service and no increase in duplicated side-effects during canary
metrics: duplication_rate_side_effects: deduplicated side-effect count / total successful responses
hedge_fanout_ratio: average number of backend fanouts per request
retry_budget_consumption: SLO token bucket fill and consumption rate per-customer
p99_request_latency: track pre- and post-hedging to ensure latency SLOs are met
failed_retry_rate: retries that still result in error after N attempts
observability_changes: Add X-Redwood-Idtok to request traces and make it redacted in logs by default
Tag hedged requests in trace span metadata (hedged=true, hedge_branch_index=n)
Emit a deduplication attribution event when a second attempt produces an already-committed side-effect
Dashboard: hedged fanout histogram, duplication_rate alert, retry_budget heatmap
testing: Unit tests for IdTok encoding/decoding validation (server treats as opaque)
Integration test: two-region failover scenario where primary times out and hedged request to secondary succeeds without duplicate side-effect
Chaos test: simulate high-latency tails and confirm hedging governor avoids explosive fanout
Load test: confirm hedging budgets prevent SLO degradation at 3x normal QPS
